value.body: The Master of Laws (LLM) is a postgraduate law degree. In India it is commonly a one-year programme (some universities still run two-year LLMs), with specialisations such as constitutional, corporate, criminal, intellectual property, international or tax law. It is mainly an academic and specialist qualification — it is not needed to practise as an advocate.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: An LLB (3-year or 5-year integrated). National Law Universities admit through CLAT-PG (some through their own tests); other universities through their own entrance tests, CUET-PG or merit.

value.title: At a glance
items: An LLM plus UGC-NET (or a PhD) is the usual route to assistant professor posts in law.
Some public-sector undertakings have used CLAT-PG scores to recruit legal officers.
For litigation and most law firms, practice experience counts more than the LLM.
LLMs abroad are often one year and expensive; their value depends on whether you plan to work or teach there.
